title: Harissa (Winter Meat Porridge)
steps: Slow-cook mutton overnight with spices until the meat is extremely tender.
Cook Kashmiri rice separately until soft.
Combine the meat and rice, then pound continuously until a smooth paste forms.
Season with green and black cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves.
Serve hot topped with smoking hot ghee and local bread.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Best enjoyed early morning during winter months .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A plate of harissa costs around INR 600-1,200 depending on the shop .

tipsList.title: Tip 3
tipsList.desc: Believed to have Persian origins, introduced to Kashmir via the Silk Route .

title: Kaladi Kulcha
steps: Heat a pan and pan-fry the Kaladi cheese in its own fat until crisp outside and gooey inside.
Lightly toast the kulchas on the pan.
Place the fried Kaladi inside the kulcha.
Top with chopped onions, tomatoes, and both green and red chutneys.
Serve immediately while hot.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Kaladi has received the GI tag .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often described as the 'mozzarella of Kashmir' for its stretchy, gooey texture .

tipsList.title: Tip 3
tipsList.desc: Can be served as a bun (Kaladi Bun) or with kulcha .

title: Gheur (Crispy Pancake)
steps: Prepare a thin batter with maida, salt, ajwain, and water.
Heat oil in a shallow pan.
Pour the batter in a lacy, circular pattern (like a crepe/pancake).
Sprinkle crushed peas and coriander on top.
Fry until crisp and golden, then serve.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: For extra flavour, consider adding a pinch of cardamom powder or other spices .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The batter consistency should be thick enough to hold its shape but not so thick that it becomes difficult to spread .

title: Rogan Josh
steps: Heat mustard oil, temper with whole spices, and sear the mutton pieces.
Add a mixture of yogurt, fennel powder, dry ginger powder, and Kashmiri red chilli.
Stir well to prevent the yogurt from splitting.
Cover and slow-cook until the mutton is completely tender.
The final gravy should be rich red and aromatic.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The red colour comes from Kashmiri chilli, not tomatoes .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best accompanied by plain or spiced basmati rice .

tipsList.title: Tip 3
tipsList.desc: Considered the dish that announces a serious meal has begun .

title: Gushtaba
steps: Pound mutton continuously with fat on a stone block until extremely smooth and spongy.
Shape the pounded meat into large meatballs.
Prepare a delicate gravy using yogurt, saffron, and mild whole spices.
Gently poach the meatballs in the boiling yogurt gravy.
Simmer until the meatballs are cooked and the gravy thickens slightly.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: No chilli fire - flavour comes from saffron and yogurt .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often called the 'grand finale' of a Wazwan banquet .

tipsList.title: Tip 3
tipsList.desc: The meat is traditionally pounded overnight on flat stones - a technique that enhances texture and flavour .

title: Rista
steps: Pound minced mutton with spices until it forms a very fine, cohesive paste.
Shape the pounded meat into small, smooth meatballs.
Prepare a vibrant red gravy using Kashmiri red chilli paste and dyer's alkanet (ratanjot).
Poach the meatballs in the red gravy.
Simmer until cooked through and tender.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: If Gushtaba is elegant, Rista is bold .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Wakes up the palate with its deep spice and luxurious mouthfeel .

title: Rajma Chawal
steps: Soak rajma overnight, then boil until tender.
Prepare a base with desi ghee, onion, ginger-garlic paste, and tomato puree.
Add spices (cinnamon, bay leaves) and the boiled rajma.
Simmer until the flavors meld and the gravy thickens.
Serve hot over rice alongside anardana chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Bhaderwah Rajma has a GI tag and is known for superior taste .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A complete vegetarian meal suitable for lunch or dinner .

title: Yakhni Mutton
steps: Boil mutton pieces with garlic, fennel, and whole spices until tender.
Strain the stock and keep the mutton aside.
Whisk yogurt with a little flour (to prevent splitting) and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the mutton pieces and the strained stock back into the yogurt.
Simmer briefly, finish with a touch of ghee and serve.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Aromatic rather than fiery - perfect for cold evenings .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The gravy is often sipped like a spiced soup .

title: Nadru Yakhni (Lotus Stem in Yogurt Gravy)
steps: Clean, slice, and parboil the lotus stem (nadru).
Whisk yogurt well and bring it to a simmer on low heat.
Add fennel powder, dry ginger powder, and cardamom.
Add the parboiled lotus stem to the yogurt base.
Simmer until the nadru is tender and absorbs the flavors.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A signature vegetarian dish of Kashmiri Pandit cuisine.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Lotus stem is prized for its crunchy texture.

title: Chaman Kaliya (Paneer Curry)
steps: Lightly pan-fry paneer cubes in ghee and soak in warm water to keep them soft.
Prepare a gravy using tomato puree, whisked yogurt, and ginger-garlic paste.
Add fennel powder, dry ginger powder, and Kashmiri chilli powder.
Add the paneer cubes to the gravy.
Simmer until the gravy thickens and coats the paneer.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A Kashmiri staple for special occasions.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The gravy should be rich, creamy and aromatic.

title: Haak (Kashmiri Collard Greens)
steps: Wash the collard greens thoroughly but keep the leaves whole.
Heat mustard oil until it smokes, then add garlic, ginger, and green chillies.
Add the haak leaves and a little water.
Cover and steam briefly so the leaves retain their vibrant green color.
Season with salt and serve.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A daily staple in Kashmiri homes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often served with rice and other dishes.

title: Dum Aloo
steps: Parboil baby potatoes, peel them, and prick with a fork.
Deep-fry the potatoes in mustard oil until golden and crisp.
Prepare a spicy yogurt-based gravy with fennel powder, dry ginger powder, and Kashmiri red chilli.
Add the fried potatoes to the gravy and seal the pot.
Cook on 'dum' (slow heat) until the potatoes absorb the flavors.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The name combines aloo (potatoes) and dum (steam/breath) - referring to the slow cooking method .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Garnished with strips of ginger and coriander leaves .

tipsList.title: Tip 3
tipsList.desc: Cooking dum aloo is considered an art because it takes a lot of time and patience .

title: Tabak Maaz
steps: Boil lamb ribs in milk with cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon until tender.
Remove the ribs and let them cool.
Heat a generous amount of ghee in a pan.
Shallow fry the boiled ribs in the ghee until the exterior is deeply crisp and brown.
Serve immediately as a hot appetizer.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Gives a wonderful contrast of textures - crispy outside, buttery within .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Usually served as an appetiser in Wazwan feasts .

title: Marchwangan Korma
steps: Heat mustard oil and sear the chicken or mutton pieces.
Add browned onions, garlic, and aromatic spices.
Prepare a fiery paste using dried Kashmiri chillies and fennel powder.
Stir the chilli paste into the meat and add water.
Simmer until the meat is cooked and the gravy is thick and intensely spicy.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Brings serious chilli character to the table - intensely red but balanced rather than scorching .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Unlike cream-heavy North Indian kormas, this one stays sharp, fragrant and oil-slicked .

title: Woste Haak te Nadru (Red Spinach with Lotus Stem)
steps: Clean and chop the red spinach; slice and parboil the lotus stem.
Heat mustard oil, temper with cumin seeds and Kashmiri chilli powder.
Add the lotus stem and sauté briefly.
Add the red spinach and beaten curd.
Cook until the spinach wilts and the lotus stem is tender.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Red spinach is usually available during winter season .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Traditionally served with steamed rice .

tipsList.title: Tip 3
tipsList.desc: Add salt and spices at the end to avoid overseasoning as leafy vegetables reduce in volume .

title: Kashmiri Pulao
steps: Soak basmati rice for 30 minutes.
Heat ghee, temper with whole spices, and sauté sliced onions until golden.
Add the soaked rice and stir gently.
Add water infused with saffron, and cook until the rice is fluffy.
Garnish generously with fried nuts, raisins, and dried fruits.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Served as part of the traditional Wazwan meal .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A popular vegetarian option on the Katra-Srinagar Vande Bharat Express .

title: Mongkhasar (Rice and Lentil Porridge)
steps: Wash and soak rice and the lentils (masoor and moong dal).
Heat mustard oil or ghee, temper with whole spices, and sauté onions and ginger-garlic.
Add the rice, lentils, powdered spices, and green chillies.
Add enough water and cook until it forms a thick, porridge-like consistency.
Serve hot with a dollop of ghee.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Keep stirring from time to time while cooking .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best served with yoghurt .

title: Ambal (Sweet and Sour Pumpkin Curry)
steps: Cube the pumpkin and set aside.
Heat mustard oil and temper with cumin, coriander, and turmeric.
Add onions and garlic, sautéing until soft.
Add the pumpkin, tamarind pulp, and jaggery.
Simmer until the pumpkin is tender and the sweet-and-sour flavors balance.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A sweet and sour pumpkin curry in Dogra style .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Also known as Ambal Kaddu .

title: Kahwa (Kashmiri Green Tea)
steps: Boil water with crushed cardamom, cinnamon, and a few saffron strands.
Add green tea leaves and turn off the heat, letting it steep briefly.
Strain the tea into cups.
Add finely slivered almonds.
Sweeten with sugar or honey as desired.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A traditional Kashmiri welcoming drink .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Served on the Katra-Srinagar Vande Bharat Express as part of the local menu .

title: Noon Chai (Kashmiri Salted Pink Tea)
steps: Boil green tea leaves in water with a pinch of baking soda until the water reduces.
Add cold water and aerate the tea by ladling it repeatedly to bring out the pink color.
Add milk and salt to taste.
Bring to a boil again.
Serve hot, often alongside traditional breads.

fullIngredients.name: Green tea leaves (specifically noon chai leaves)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The pink colour comes from the reaction of baking soda with the tea.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often served with Kashmiri bread like kulcha or girda.

tipsList.title: Tip 3
tipsList.desc: A staple in Kashmiri households, especially during winter.

title: Modur Pulao (Kashmiri Sweet Pulao)
steps: Cook basmati rice until just tender.
In a separate pan, heat ghee and temper with cardamom.
Add milk, sugar, and saffron to make a sweet syrup.
Gently fold the cooked rice into the sweet syrup.
Garnish heavily with fried nuts, raisins, and fried onions.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A festive sweet pulao often served at weddings.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The caramelized onions give it a distinctive sweet flavour.
